drop_off_rule: Show items published within the last 7 days. Remove any item more than 14 days after its date_published, even if fewer than 10 items remain.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast agentic model at $1.50/$7.50 per million tokens, plus Orchestrator in Antigravity
items.summary: Hydrogen is Google's new fast model for everyday coding and agent work, scoring 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default setting (one point above Argon), with a flat-priced 1 million-token context, four thinking levels, and availability today in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Search.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customers on Gemini 3.8 Flash have a clear upgrade path (Google reports 2.5x faster tasks and 57% vs 18.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1), and the Carbon-plans, Hydrogen-executes split is a ready pattern for cutting cost on multi-agent deployments; rerun your own evals before switching.

items.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed customer data, including Notion AI chat transcripts
items.summary: Fireworks AI confirmed an attacker got into a development system through its cloud provider and took billing information and some customer datasets; Notion says about 1% of its customers were affected, including Notion AI Insights chat inputs and outputs, and it cut its connection to Fireworks on Nov 3.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: If a customer routes prompts through Fireworks or any inference provider, check what data that provider stores and for how long, and rotate any keys there; this is the second Fireworks incident in two months.

items.title: United Airlines blocks third-party AI agents from booking flights and managing reservations
items.summary: United says it is restricting unauthorized personal AI agents on its own platforms and through travel agencies and aggregators, citing the risk of shared credentials and federal rules that require a human to complete steps like check-in.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Agents that act on a user's logged-in accounts are hitting policy walls at airlines and banks, so design customer agents around sanctioned APIs and partner channels rather than shared passwords, and keep a human step where regulations require it.

items.title: Google launches the Gemini Decisions API and Gemini Decision 1 for fast, calibrated yes/no, choice and rubric decisions
items.summary: The new Gemini API endpoint scores up to 1,000 closed-set questions (yes/no, multiple choice, rubric) against one text, image, audio, video or PDF input in a single pass, returning probabilities and confidence in about 150-250 ms at $0.10 per million input tokens with no output tokens billed.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Routing, policy checks and triage steps you now do with prompt-and-parse JSON calls can move to a cheaper, faster endpoint with a confidence score you can threshold to send unsure cases to a human; it's in Google AI Studio and Vercel AI Gateway now, but not yet in Gemini on Google Cloud.

items.title: Hugging Face adds decision models to Transformers and llama.cpp, served on a shared /v1/systemone API
items.summary: Hugging Face's guide shows open-weight decision models (the category TypeSafe started with Jev) running through a new Transformers "decision" pipeline, with transformers serve and llama.cpp both exposing the same /v1/systemone endpoint that returns structured choices with probabilities instead of generated text.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: For customers who can't send data to a hosted API, you can now run the same routing and classification pattern on their own hardware with a standard endpoint, but you still need to calibrate thresholds per question before trusting the probabilities.

items.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon generally available, with /swarm multi-agent teams previewing in Antigravity
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's strongest model for long-horizon coding, research and cyber work, is now on the paid Gemini API, Gemini for business and Google AI Ultra at an introductory $2/$10 per million tokens through Nov 30 (then $4/$20), and Antigravity's new /swarm turns one prompt into a coordinated team of agents.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Carbon undercuts Fable 5.2 on per-token price, so benchmark it on your customers' hardest agent workloads before Nov 30 and budget for the price doubling; Google itself says Argon is still the better default for most work.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia's board said Huang resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately after reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, and CFO Colette Kress is leading the company while it searches for a successor, with earnings due Tuesday.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Nothing changes in your stack today, but watch Tuesday's earnings call for any shift in GPU supply, pricing or Nvidia's open-model and software commitments before you lock customer infrastructure plans.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings, Whiteboards and Sheets, and makes Claude Data generally available
items.summary: Claude can now join Google Meet calls as a visible participant (beta, Team and Enterprise), build shared whiteboards and spreadsheets with teams (beta, paid plans), and answer questions from a connected warehouse or CRM through Claude Data, alongside interactive connectors that open apps like Adobe, Atlassian and HubSpot inside Claude.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Check customer Enterprise org settings now: Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default there, but Claude Data turns on by default on Nov 19, and Meetings leaves calls when an external guest joins unless an admin allows it.

items.title: OpenAI launches Businesses in ChatGPT, letting companies claim profiles and run their own Business Agents
items.summary: Through Business Hub, companies can claim and verify their ChatGPT listing, add product feeds and see aggregated engagement insights, and eligible US ecommerce and online service businesses can now build a Business Agent that shoppers chat with inside ChatGPT.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Customer-facing agents now have a distribution channel inside ChatGPT, so retail and services customers will ask for help claiming their listing, keeping feeds accurate and building a Business Agent.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 to everyone, with Mythos 5.2 gated to verified cyber and life-sciences orgs
items.summary: Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are the same model with different safeguards; Fable 5.2 is out now on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Azure as claude-fable-5-2 at $8/$40 per million tokens, up to 30% faster than 5.1, with an optional fast mode at $16/$80.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Anthropic's top model is now cheaper and on every major cloud, so re-run your customer evals and cost estimates on claude-fable-5-2, and route security or biomedical customers to the Verification Programs if they need Mythos.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 is GA in GitHub Copilot, but admins must opt in and it requires data retention by default
items.summary: Fable 5.2 is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise across VS Code, the CLI, the coding agent and more; the org policy is off by default because Anthropic retains prompts and outputs for safety classifiers, with a zero-data-retention exemption for eligible enterprises through year end.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Before turning Fable on for a customer's Copilot org, check their data-retention rules; enabling the policy counts as accepting retention, and ZDR eligibility only goes through the GitHub account team.

items.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code agents formally verified Signal's protocol implementation in four weeks
items.summary: A multi-agent framework built on Gemini Carbon wrote over six million lines of Lean to prove key security properties of Signal's actual compiled cryptographic code, leaving about 1% for human review, and DeepMind is open-sourcing the verification artifacts.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Agent-driven formal verification is moving from research toward production code, which is worth knowing for security-sensitive customers who ask how far AI code assurance can go.

items.title: ChatGPT Enterprise is now sold through AWS Marketplace
items.summary: Organizations can buy and manage ChatGPT Enterprise, plus ChatGPT for Healthcare and Financial Services, through their AWS billing and apply eligible spend to AWS commitments, alongside OpenAI models already in Amazon Bedrock.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: For AWS-committed customers, procurement for ChatGPT Enterprise can now go through their existing AWS contract, which can shorten deal cycles.

items.title: Conductor is joining Meta, and Conductor Cloud shuts down on November 20
items.summary: Conductor, the Mac app for running parallel Claude Code and Codex agents, stopped new sign-ups on Nov 4; its cloud workspaces go read-only Nov 13 and cloud data deletion begins Nov 20, while the local app gets fixes until early 2027.
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: If you or a customer run agents in Conductor Cloud, use Transfer to local or Settings > Account > Export data before Nov 13, and plan a replacement for parallel-agent workflows before the local app winds down.

items.title: Claude Code was putting users' account emails into User-Agent headers; Anthropic is removing them from model context
items.summary: Claude Code sometimes put the signed-in account email into User-Agent on web or curl calls after Anthropic added that email to model context; a built-in privacy mod landed in 2.1.317+, and Anthropic says a release early next week will stop putting the email in context.
items.source: Anthropic Claude Code (GitHub issue + staff confirmation)
items.why_it_matters_for_FDEs: Any customer running Claude Code with web tools should update to 2.1.317+, keep the privacy mod on, and audit agent network egress until the context fix ships, because leaked work emails create spam and compliance exposure.
